hypotheses.reasoning: notif-worker crashes deterministically on msg-364842 at Kafka-style offset 371126 of notifications.outbound: expandReferences throws RangeError (call stack overflow). Each restart resumes at the same committed offset (#2010, #2102, #2267, #2553), so the consumer re-hits the same message and crash-loops with growing backoff (10s, 20s, 40s, 80s). The loop is the message being re-consumed, not a resource or deploy problem. The lag rising on notifications.outbound is explained by this consumer being stuck. Alternative considered: GC pauses (#1815, 1069ms) are minor and not the crash cause; the crash is a stack overflow from one payload's recursive references. Other errors (events-db lock timeouts, enrichment-svc timeouts, report-cron pandas ModuleNotFoundError, metrics-agent queue drops) are separate, unrelated symptoms in other services and do not touch notif-worker.

Alternative reading: the message payload is malformed or has circular references that were written upstream, making it data_integrity rather than a consumer-side poison message. Only msg-364842 is affected, so the payload is the trigger either way; the fix is the same, skip or dead-letter the offset and fix the upstream record.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or dead-letter msg-364842 at offset 371126 on notifications.outbound (move it to a DLQ after saving the payload), so notif-worker can advance past it and drain the lag. Then fix expandReferences to handle deep or circular references, or add a recursion guard, and find which upstream producer emitted the malformed payload. Separately, track the unrelated issues: report-cron's nightly-revenue-report is failing because pandas is missing from image report-cron:2026.10.2, and enrichment-svc / events-db have lock and statement timeouts causing ingest-api and ingest-gateway 504s.
